dataset.name: automotive::generate_catalog(4500) split by index range into a 1500-product calibration slice and a 3000-product held-out slice, plus hand-built extension cases (collision, absent identifier, legitimate cross-reference, adversarial near-miss, 7-variant stress product); mixed_merchant's 3000-product mixed catalog used for a real, executed general-lexical-regression check (added second correction round -- see below); plus several small, dedicated synthetic catalogs at fixed variants-per-product levels (1/3/7/15, 200 products each) for the variants-per-product build/incremental-update scaling curve (added second correction round)

engine_config.note: none of these route through commerce_core::plan::execute_planned/LexicalDelegate -- LexicalHit cannot express a resolved VariantId at all, see ISSUE42_PROTOCOL.md's dated correction

repetitions: 5 independent full runs; every correctness/classification/recall/false-match/violation number is byte-identical across all 5 (confirmed by direct diff); latency, build time, incremental-update time, and RSS deltas vary run-to-run and are reported as ranges (including a disclosed bimodal split for Treatment B's incremental-update cost), not a single favorable run

headline_result.treatment_a: finds 0 of 2972 held-out identifiers -- part_number is variant-level only and phase9_eval::bitmap_delegate::build_index never indexes anything beyond product-level Text/title. Confirms H3-A.
headline_result.treatment_b: 100% Recall@1 / 0% false-match on the genuinely-unique held-out sample, correctly surfaces both variants of a deliberate collision, but matches a bare prefix query it should reject -- confirming H3-B's own predicted weakness directly.
headline_result.treatment_c: matches B's Recall@1/false-match numbers exactly (100%/0%) on the one field (part_number) it accepts, correctly rejects the prefix and adversarial near-miss queries, and builds/updates substantially faster than B in every one of 5 independent runs (build ~2.3-2.6ms vs B's ~12.6-18.4ms; incremental update ~0.0008-0.0023ms vs B's bimodal ~6.5-6.7ms/~104.8-107.4ms). Every other field present in the held-out catalog (17 of 18, including a deliberately-added 'legitimate cross-reference' field with only 2 occurrences sharing one value) correctly ABSTAINS, falling back to Treatment B exactly as the protocol's own abstention behavior requires, now gated on both uniqueness ratio AND variant scope (see second_correction_round). Confirms H3-C. PASSES every preregistered R3 GO-gate criterion.
headline_result.verdict: GO for Treatment C. Mirroring R2's own outcome (unlike R1's REVISE), Treatment C's calibrated-classifier-plus-dictionary mechanism clears every preregistered GO-gate criterion. Per Issue #42's own rule, this is a real candidate for a RED-before-GREEN production change to commerce_core -- deliberately not made in this same pass. A fresh, no-implementation-task adversarial reviewer must first attempt to falsify this protocol/fixture/code/arithmetic/claim and every confirmed finding independently reproduced and fixed, before that change is made; the production-change step itself is tracked separately (task #63, after R1/R2), so R1/R2/R3's serving-contract decisions are reviewed together.
headline_result.reproducibility: all 5 runs byte-identical on every correctness/classification/recall/false-match/violation number (verified by direct diff excluding the build_time_ms/incremental_update_ms/rss_delta_kb/index_size_bytes_b JSON fields)
headline_result.preregistration_corrections: Two found before any treatment code was written, both dated in ISSUE42_PROTOCOL.md: (1) automotive::generate_catalog has no seed parameter at all, so the protocol's literal calibration/held-out split text was unachievable, and a naive two-call workaround would have made calibration a byte-identical prefix of held-out -- fixed via one generate_catalog(4500) call split by index range into disjoint slices; (2) commerce_core::plan::LexicalHit has no VariantId field and verify_and_truncate's per-variant resolution is vacuously true whenever query.constraints is empty (exactly the identifier-only-query case, since compile() has no 'part number' keyword branch) -- so today's real pipeline always returns a product's first variant regardless of which variant matched; every R3 treatment is therefore its own self-contained index-and-lookup path with a real, variant-aware hit type instead.
headline_result.self_caught_methodology_bug: The initial Recall@1/false-match sample counted every naturally-occurring identifier collision (automotive's own real RNG draw occasionally repeating by chance, the same phenomenon the calibration set's own 0.998 uniqueness ratio already showed) as a false match whenever the sample iterated to one collision-partner and the top hit resolved to the other -- conflating a genuine, correctly-surfaced collision (separately tested and passing via the dedicated collision case) with an actual wrong resolution, producing an initial false read of 'Treatment C FAILS the GO gate' (0.37% false-match) purely from test-methodology, not a real defect. Fixed by excluding catalog-wide-non-unique identifiers (22 of 2994 candidates, disclosed) from the sample; both B and C then measure exactly 100%/0%. A second, unrelated determinism bug (shannon_entropy_bits summing floating-point terms in HashMap's randomized iteration order) was also self-caught by diffing 5 runs before trusting a byte-identical claim, and fixed via BTreeMap's deterministic order. Both caught and fixed before any adversarial review, following the same discipline R1/R2 established for self-caught bugs.
headline_result.second_correction_round: A fresh adversarial reviewer with no implementation task, before any production change was made on the strength of R3's GO verdict, independently recomputed every number/claim from the raw artifacts and source and found four substantive issues plus one minor one, all independently reproduced before being fixed: (1) IdentifierClassifier::accepts silently narrowed the protocol's own preregistered multi-signal classifier design down to uniqueness ratio alone, with no dated deviation note; (2) a concrete consequence -- lumens (a genuine non-identifier Numeric attribute) scored uniqueness_ratio=0.94 on calibration, only 0.01 below the 0.95 cutoff (0.89 on the 2x-larger held-out set, i.e. a sample-size artifact, not semantic identifier-ness), a real margin risk a single-signal classifier has no second check against. A first candidate fix (gating on a new format_consistency/character-class-signature statistic) was tested with real numbers before being adopted and found to EMPIRICALLY FAIL -- it scored part_number itself at only ~0.51-0.56, lower than several genuine non-identifiers, because automotive's own brand/type names vary in word count, so part_number's own code segments vary in length too; gating on it would have incorrectly rejected the true identifier field. This negative result is recorded (per CLAUDE.md's 'record failed experiments'), not erased -- both format_consistency and a fixed-length-ratio variant remain computed and reported but do not gate. The real, structurally-justified fix: require variant_scoped (already computed, previously unused) in addition to uniqueness ratio -- automotive's generator sets part_number/warranty_months/compatible_fitment directly on Variant, every other attribute (lumens included) only on Product -- verified to produce identical classification results to before on both calibration and held-out sets, with no new false accept. (3) Build-time/incremental-update cost had only been measured at one variants-per-product level; fixed by adding r3_workload::build_scaling_catalog and a new scaling-curve section measuring Treatments B/C independently at 4 dedicated levels (1/3/7/15 variants-per-product, 200 products each) -- Treatment C's build time scales roughly linearly with total variant count as expected of a per-entry HashMap insert; Treatment B's incremental-update cost shows the same bimodal split already disclosed at the main held-out-catalog scale recurring at every tested level, ruling out variants-per-product itself as the trigger. (4) The general-lexical-regression check had been argued (a built-then-discarded catalog) rather than measured; fixed by exposing HeldOutMixed's real product_types/brands/categories and running a real commerce_core::index::CatalogIndex::execute_ranked check against 3 real free-text queries twice, asserting byte-identical hit counts. (5, minor) the console print and JSON summary read index_b.index_size_bytes() at two different points in the run, silently reporting two different byte counts under one label; fixed by capturing one consistent post-build snapshot (129,315 bytes, superseding the originally-published 129,713 -- both recorded, not silently replaced). None of these fixes reverses the GO verdict: Treatment C still clears every preregistered R3 GO-gate criterion, confirmed across 5 freshly regenerated runs, byte-identical on every correctness/classification field. Full detail: docs/experiments/ISSUE42_LOG.md's 'Second correction round' section under I42-R3.
